analysis.title: Market Internal Insight: Rebecca's On-the-Road Observations + $77 Excess Buy Flow Today
key_insights: UBS US Equity Derivatives desk says today's flows suggest the anticipated weakness ahead of the Thursday IPO is close to ending, unless more cyber attacks and outages trigger further retail anxiety and an unwind.
Client demand for UBS data (DL requests) reached 120+ in two weeks versus a normal 50-80 per month, which the desk reads as unusually high investor anxiety and uncertainty.
IPO analog: SPX fell -5.8% on average in the three weeks before a major IPO and rallied +9.5% on average over the next three months. SPX is -5.2% over the last three weeks, in line with history.

Trend vs volatility framework: the major trend is set by retail investors (42% of US equity ownership) and foreign investors (18%), together 60% of US equities. Volatility around the trend comes from a downside feedback loop after headline shocks, driven by hedge funds, systematic funds (risk control, CTA, risk parity), leveraged ETPs, short covering and some 0dte options.

Fast-money positioning is washed out, with UBS PB L/S net exposure near a 5-year low. Risk control, CTA and leveraged ETP exposures sit at the 2%, 5% and 11%-tile versus 1 year. An intraday -2% drawdown is therefore less likely to turn into -4% on the same day through quant feedback.

Before today, retail bought the dip in 3 of 3 down days and 7 of the last 8 down days, and foreigners bought at over +4x standard deviation. The desk reads this as an upside trend bias once volatility subsides.
Retail sold the dip modestly today. The desk says the upside implication holds as long as retail selling does not last more than 2 days.

Based on UBS RMM intraday flow and stock flow bias since 2013, retail bought the dip about 65-70% of the time. Retail does not sell on bad earnings or routine monthly/quarterly economic releases. FOMC is a maybe.

Retail sell triggers listed by the desk: the start of a new phenomenon creating social anxiety, the start of a new war, the announcement (not implementation) of tariffs, the start of Covid, a large Bitcoin drop causing margin calls, and a sell-off that falls more than 10% after retail starts buying. The desk's own unobserved views add very high unemployment and very high inflation.
Excess buy flow was +$77 bn despite SPX -1.0%. This is the first buy flow over $50 bn on an SPX decline of more than 50 bps since March 3, 2026.

VIX Cross-Asset Rank peaked at 98% intraday and closed at 94%, with VIX at 26. The desk calls this a typically over-hedged condition and says a reading above 95% is usually strong intraday resistance or an overbought condition.

UBS RMM clients sold the dip modestly, with net flow at the 18%-tile versus 3 years, the first time in the last 4 down sessions. The desk links this to anxiety over outages and hacking, and expects a return to dip-buying unless outages continue back-to-back.
CTA equity exposure turned negative after 2 sell triggers crossed in both ES1 and RTY1. Two MA crossover sell triggers for RTY1 are expected within 1 and 3 days.
Leveraged ETP rebalance was -$3.7 bn to sell, including -$1.9 bn in Nasdaq and tech and -$1.6 bn in QQQ.
Selling was concentrated in tech: Nasdaq excess sell flow was -$1 bn with QQQ -0.7%. Retail sell tilt was in internet and e-commerce, hardware and software.
crypto_views: The desk lists a large Bitcoin drop that triggers margin calls and forces retail to sell equities to fund margin accounts as one of the conditions under which retail sells the dip.
risk_factors: Further cyber attacks and outages could raise retail anxiety and trigger a retail unwind.
Retail dip-selling lasting more than 2 days would remove the upside implication the desk draws from retail flows.
CTA equity exposure has turned negative, and more sell triggers are expected in RTY1 within 1 to 3 days.
The Thursday IPO may absorb cash from the market before the post-IPO redeployment the desk expects.
vol_and_positioning: VIX at 26. VIX Cross-Asset Rank peaked at 98% intraday (after 11:32 am) and closed at 94%, after 87% the previous day. A reading above 95% is usually strong intraday resistance or an overbought condition.
UBS PB L/S net exposure is near a 5-year low. Risk control, CTA and leveraged ETP exposures are at the 2%, 5% and 11%-tile versus 1 year.
ES1: 2 sell triggers crossed at 10:34 am and 10:40 am, with no close buy or sell trigger within 2%. The first buy trigger is at 7630.9 (+3.5% from current).
RTY1: 2 sell triggers crossed at 1:35 am and 4:19 am. There is no close buy trigger within 2%. Two close MA crossover sell triggers are expected by the end of the week.
NQ1: no trigger crossed today and no close buy or sell trigger within 2%. The first buy trigger is at 28607 (+5.3% from current).
Leveraged ETP rebalance of -$3.7 bn to sell, including -$1.9 bn in Nasdaq and tech and -$1.6 bn in QQQ.
Basket returns: the worst were Solar Energy (-6.0%), Software AI Risk (-4.5%), AI Risk (-4.1%), Software & SaaS (-3.8%) and Speculative Growth (-3.5%). The best was Gold Miners (+0.8%).

tension_points.bull_case: Washed-out fast-money positioning, +$77 bn excess buy flow, an over-hedged VIX Cross-Asset Rank and the post-IPO analog (+9.5% over 3 months) point to the end of the weakness and an upside trend driven by retail and foreign buying.
tension_points.bear_case: Retail sold the dip today for the first time in 4 down sessions, CTA exposure turned negative with more RTY1 sell triggers due, and further cyber attacks or outages could extend retail anxiety and selling.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Retail dip-selling lasting more than 2 days, or more back-to-back outages and cyber attacks that keep retail anxiety elevated.
